v2 widened it, still stratified by declared size, and found ONE.
Reason: Constraint 6 establishes that ALL 440 declared sizes are KiB-exact,
i.e. quantised. A sample stratified on a quantised field cannot see the thing
the sample is for. pvd0RJrB - a confirmed genuine-stereo unit - carries a
declared size of exactly 2 GiB, so it fell into the sentinel bucket, and the
sentinel bucket received the SMALLEST allocation. The sentinel defect again:
not as a threshold, not as a cost, not as a peak, but as a SAMPLING FRAME.

CONSEQUENCE_FOR_THE_MONEY.the_2x_bill_is_REAL: 2 of 65 = 3.08% of sampled calls would be billed at 2x. Projected onto 191 dated calls that is ~6 calls, ~$35 extra - NOT the $197.68 worst case, which remains the correct ceiling to hold against.
CONSEQUENCE_FOR_THE_MONEY.THE -ac 1 SAVING IS NOT UNCONDITIONAL: The $34.85 saving is proven lossless on a bit-identical dual-mono source (nhbplus-w0-aclose) and is DEMONSTRABLY NOT LOSSLESS on the two genuine-stereo files above. This is exactly why section 7.1a branches on channel topology instead of downmixing everything, and it is the reason the INDEPENDENT and AMBIGUOUS branches must not be deleted on the strength of a sample that found no stereo.
CONSEQUENCE_FOR_THE_MONEY.the_branch_is_not_dead_code: Section 7.1a's keep-stereo branch FIRES on 2 of 65. Section 2.2's keep-stereo budget line stands.

A_PROCESS_FAILURE_WORTH_RECORDING: The first v3 run terminated at 25 of 65 and produced rows whose handles did
not match their results. Cause: EVERY command inside a `while read` loop must
have stdin closed. ffmpeg and ffprobe READ STDIN by default, and only
mega-get had been guarded - so ffmpeg consumed the loop's remaining input
and the row labels drifted from the rows.
This is the SAME family as v2's resolver IndexError and as the two-unit field
join that started this whole exercise: a pipeline step silently operating on
the wrong item. It was caught only because one handle produced two opposite
verdicts across two runs. All pre-fix v3 rows were discarded, not averaged.
